title: Record the no-blind-import rule as its own module

costar.context: The maintainer said foreign code is never pulled in blindly. This build codes, aligns, and specs each intake.
costar.objective: Keep that rule as a plug-in module the checker discovers from module.json.
costar.style: One folder with a skill, a spec schema, and one decision record.
costar.audience: The next coding agent and the maintainer.
costar.response: A canon module, a pointer in the always-on operating rule, and organize.py --check exiting 0 with six modules.

concerns: A schema that allows any string for decision would accept an import. The spec enum is write-here or reject, and a check_node call must reject import.
Raising the self-test module floor would hardcode the module count. The floor stays at 6, which the probe still exceeds.
Editing organize.py to name canon would break plug-and-play. The checker must not gain a canon line.
context: Five context modules already exist. The user required that outside code be rewritten here against our specs and practices.
current_state: organize.py discovers every .ai/modules/<id>/module.json, requires SKILL.md, schema/, and data/, and does not list module ids except the journal writer. ai-operating.mdc lists five skills. There is no canon folder.
target_design: canon is the sixth module. Adding it is a folder plus one bullet in the always-on rule. The checker source does not mention canon.
changes: Create .ai/modules/canon with module.json, SKILL.md, schema/intake.schema.json, and data/no-blind-import.json.
Add the canon skill path to .cursor/rules/ai-operating.mdc.
Add canon to the PROTOCOL.md module table.
Store this plan and set the COSTAR reading to this decision.
boundaries: Do not change Cargo.toml features or the license field.
Do not mark the build phase done.
Do not add a license validator.
Do not commit or push in this pass.

verification.name: import-is-rejected-and-probe-is-discovered
verification.command: python -c "import organize" from .ai/machine rejecting decision import; python .ai/machine/organize.py --self-test
verification.proves: The intake spec refuses decision import, and a temporary module is still discovered without a registry edit.
verification.expected: import rejected; self-test exit 0, ok true, modules 7
verification.result: rejected bad.decision: 'import' not in ['write-here', 'reject']; self-test {"ok": true, "modules": 7, "documents": 7, "events": 178, "messages": 69, "tools": 329, "journal": 2}

verification.name: six-modules-match-their-schemas
verification.proves: Canon and the five existing modules all match their schemas, including the write-here intake and this plan once it has results.
